comments.value: Nothing is safe you make public or bring to public in VRChat.
Content of any game can be stolen/ripped, and devs can't do anything about it.
As others stated, this isn't specifically a VRChat issue, you can download tools to rip scenes, models, and textures from any Unity game with ease.
It's kinda hard to fix when you can just take stuff right from your cache

but the problem is that you can convert a vrchat cache file to a compressed unity file without any tools. So it's almost impossible to control and to police people that upload stolen content is not a easy matter either. It's a cost vs benefit thing unfortunately

It would be nice if the .vrca files were encrypted or at least obfuscated in such a way that it would be extremely difficult to successfully crack the files off VRC's servers. For direct asset theft and the like, that's on the users to file a DMCA complaint. They are US based so they have to follow the us DMCA. If you take this route, VRChat has a legal obligation to investigate or they could be sued for infringement from the asset owner. Just be aware that you have to be the owner or legally allowed to act on behalf of the owner before filing such a complaint.

The issue is that if some sort of script is implemented, the client will be decompiled and deobfuscated anyway. Then the script will be available to read for anyone. The theft is added into a hacked client after any download, decompression, or "theft avoidance" system.

You realize most VRChat avatars are stolen intellectual property to begin with? :p

And sure, they could try to do something about it, but so long as the game can 'decode' whatever they're doing, someone can just find out what the game does and do it themselves.
@rivus-play: Agreed. And the fact they haven't done anything about it is a total joke.
@{5ae5c147906bfd12e600dc47|full_name}: Downloading publicly available models and assets from sites like deviantart and bowlroll is not "stealing" intellectual property.

@{5b6b4e8cb1b04a6db0be465d|full_name}: Depending on the license, it can be!
Same as 'downloading' code from a GitHub page.

@{5bd4da95a5c5264bf3199faf|full_name}: They are encrypted, it's just the encryption key is publicly knowledge so it does nothing. Also, as long as people can mod their clients, people can just steal the raw FBX during loading anyway, no .vrca file needed. Honestly need anticheat... Dx

@{5b6b4e8cb1b04a6db0be465d|full_name}: It depends on the author's license as some authors disallow the modification of their mdoels specifically for use in VRChat. TDA has a clause in their license agreements for the Vocaloid models which is supposed to disallow such use.
